panels.description: Routing-plan estimate: fraction of locally owned in-flight input tokens that GWP's approximate indexer expected to be cached on its selected worker, broken down by routed cluster. This is not an execution-observed worker cache-hit rate. The axis is fixed at 0–1.
panels.title: Indexer-Estimated Cache Hit Ratio by Cluster (Routing Plan)

panels.description: Execution-observed prefix-cache hit rate reported by each Dynamo engine worker through dynamo_component_kv_cache_hit_rate. The lines summarize the distribution across workers; unlike the adjacent panel, this is not GWP's routing-plan estimate.
panels.title: Worker-Reported KV Cache Hit Rate (Execution)

panels.description: Responses completed at the client-facing Envoy listener, grouped by HTTP status class. This is Envoy's boundary view and includes requests that may not reach GWP. It is intentionally independent of model and routed-endpoint filters.
panels.title: Envoy Response Results

panels.description: End-to-end request duration measured by the client-facing Envoy listener, from downstream request arrival through response completion. Envoy reports this histogram in milliseconds; the queries convert it to seconds. Time to first byte remains available in Envoy's structured access logs via RESPONSE_DURATION.
panels.title: Envoy End-to-End Response Time

panels.description: Low-cardinality outcomes from Envoy's native ext_authz scheduling filter and Rust Wasm lifecycle adapter. denied is a non-2xx GWP scheduling decision; error is a native transport failure or timeout; invalid is a malformed authorization response. Lifecycle dispatch failures are asynchronous and do not delay the client stream.
panels.title: Envoy GWP Control Outcomes

panels.description: Native Envoy ext_authz filter-state latency for the body-bearing gRPC Check call. This is the external schedule round trip: loopback transport, protobuf body transfer, GWP queueing, affinity lookup, tokenization/selection when needed, booking, and response encoding. The envoy_grpc client does not populate cluster upstream_rq_time, so this panel intentionally uses envoy_gwp_schedule_round_trip_time. Below 20 ms is healthy; 20–100 ms is degraded and above 100 ms warrants investigation.

targets.expr: clamp_min(histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (rate(envoy_gwp_schedule_round_trip_time_bucket{namespace=~"$namespace"}[$__rate_interval]))) / 1000 - 1000 * histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (rate(dynamo_component_gwp_schedule_service_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace=~"$namespace",adapter="ext_authz"}[$__rate_interval]))), 0)

panels.title: Envoy → GWP Schedule Round-Trip Time

panels.description: Successful affinity peek latency on the scheduling critical path, measured inside GWP's instrumented backend wrapper. Compare this directly with the adjacent Envoy-observed schedule RTT to identify Redis/etcd contribution. Timeout and bulkhead outcomes remain visible in the affinity error panels.
panels.title: Affinity Store Peek Latency

panels.description: Time spent inside GWP converting the OpenAI request into routing tokens. Real includes chat-template rendering and tokenizer execution; pseudo includes routing-text rendering and byte-chunk token generation.

targets.expr: 1000 * histogram_quantile(0.50, sum by (le, model, mode, result) (rate(dynamo_component_gwp_tokenization_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace=~"$namespace",model=~"$model"}[$__rate_interval])))
1000 * histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, model, mode, result) (rate(dynamo_component_gwp_tokenization_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace=~"$namespace",model=~"$model"}[$__rate_interval])))
1000 * histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, model, mode, result) (rate(dynamo_component_gwp_tokenization_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace=~"$namespace",model=~"$model"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: GWP Tokenization Latency

panels.description: Internal GWP schedule latency split by path. optimistic_affinity returns before tokenization, prefix hashing, index lookup, and scheduler booking; synchronous_affinity and scored_selection include those operations.
panels.title: GWP Schedule Latency by Path

panels.description: Rates of bounded background-tokenization outcomes. Active jobs use the right axis and should remain at or below four per replica; saturated_fallback means the request used synchronous scheduling instead of entering an unbounded queue.
panels.title: Optimistic Sticky Scheduling Outcomes

panels.description: Complete GWP control-service time from request arrival through body ingestion, JSON extraction, scheduling, and response encoding. Compare with Envoy schedule RTT to locate proxy/transport overhead. Quantile subtraction in the RTT panel is approximate because histogram observations are not paired.
panels.title: GWP Complete Schedule Service Time

panels.description: Schedule request body size observed by the native gRPC ext-authz service from the protobuf raw body. Instrumentation does not re-buffer the request body.
panels.title: GWP Schedule Request Body Size
